top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a mature, independently confirmed discovery: Kane and Mele's Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state, and Molenkamp's observation of the predicted helical edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells. Band inversion from spin-orbit coupling was computed from first principles, used to choose the material and then verified. It is distinct from the 2016 prize on topological phases in model systems. The Mele-for-Hasan allocation follows the 2D logic of the discovery, and the omissions of Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and of Hasan's 3D work must be stated openly with a narrow citation. P002 (Katori and Ye) has the cleaner credit boundary but overlaps the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, so it ranks second. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye. Scientific proximity only through first-principles electronic-structure and magnetism work.
